# Exposure results (7 days)

**SIMULATED DATA.** Generated by `scripts/build_results_pack.py` from the materialised exposure tables (engine exposure-1.1). Personal figures are `estimated_personal`; dust is `indicative`; WBGT is `approximate` (an underestimate). Methods and assumptions: `docs/exposure_methods.md`.

Shift dates 2026-10-20 → 2026-10-26; 140 worker-sessions, 140 with valid noise data.

## Distribution across worker-days

| | min | p25 | median | p75 | max |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| NIOSH dose % | 13.1 | 244.0 | 444.7 | 1,294.6 | 3,515.3 |
| India dose % | 0.2 | 25.7 | 88.9 | 207.7 | 425.1 |
| L_EX,8h (dBA) | 76.2 | 88.8 | 91.5 | 96.1 | 100.4 |

## Worker-days above 100% dose

- NIOSH: **126 / 140 (90.0%)**
- India: **56 / 140 (40.0%)**

## Data quality

- Mean data coverage **99.06%** (minimum 96.47%)
- Mean unaccounted time **0.15%** (maximum 0.32%)
- Anomaly-flagged readings excluded: 3,284; ≥115 dBA readings among them (listed, not dropped): 20; genuine ≥115 dBA events: 0

## Deterministic risk index

> The weights are a design choice of this project, not a validated clinical model. The respiratory component is relative to the cohort, not to a health threshold. Label: `deterministic_index`.

- 140 worker-days; index min 11.0, median 71.7, max 82.2
- Bands: High 110, Low 14, Medium 16
- Hearing uses L_EX,8h (75 → 105 dBA maps to 0 → 100; risk-1.1). risk-1.0 used dose % capped at 100%, which saturated; the dose under both criteria is always shown beside the index. The rating is mostly High because this is a loud mill (`exposure_methods.md` §8).
